newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Four Brazil courts rule against CVRD sale so far.
newsitem.headline: Four Brazil courts rule against CVRD sale so far.

text.p: Four regional Brazilian courts have issued injunctions so far against Tuesday's scheduled privatization of mining company Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), officials said.

A spokeswoman for the National Development Bank (BNDES) said a court in Rio de Janeiro had issued two injunctions and courts in the states of Maranhao and Ceara one each. A Sao Paulo court on Friday issued the first of the injunctions.
"Our lawyers have already lodged appeals," the spokeswoman said on Monday, adding it was "completely unpredictable" how long it would take to have the injunctions revoked.
Forty-five percent of CVRD's voting shares are due to go on the auction block in the Rio de Janeiro bolsa at 1000 local/1300 GMT Tuesday.
The country's highest court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), on Monday rejected two applications for injunctions against the privatization, one questioning its constitutionality.
Government officials said they were confident they could successfully appeal the injunctions granted regionally in time to allow the auction to proceed on schedule.
But they have acknowledged they are concerned about a Rio de Janeiro judge ruling on a case brought by 12 public prosecutors, acting as private citizens.
The judge, Salete Maccaloz, was working on the case, a secretary said.
A Sao Paulo judge considering a government appeal against the injunction granted there was also still studying his case, officials there said.
